articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts a missile as fighting rages in Yemen’s al-Jawf
articles.summary: Houthi-affiliated media report that seven people were wounded in strikes on the city of Hodeidah.
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen says air defences intercepted a Houthi missile, while fighting continues to rage along key fronts between the armed group and forces loyal to the internationally recognised Yemeni government.

Defences “intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile” targeting Saudi Arabia’s southern region, said coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki in a statement on Monday.

Earlier, he said defences destroyed a drone launched toward the southern region on Sunday evening.

Also on Monday, the Saudi Civil Defence authority issued and then lifted alerts warning of “potential danger” in the city of Abha, as well as the provinces of Khamis Mushait, Taif and Najran.

The authority warned residents against “filming, publishing or sharing information” related to missile and drone attacks.

In Yemen, a media outlet affiliated with the Houthi armed group, also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), reported that seven people were wounded in Saudi-led coalition air strikes on Hodeidah on the Red Sea coast.

Four people were wounded in the attacks on Ras Isa port dock, while three others suffered injuries in a strike on an oil company site in the governorate’s Bajil district, Houthi media reported.

There was no comment on the reports from the Saudi-led coalition.

The latest clashes come as Yemeni government forces keep up their campaign to regain positions from the Iran-aligned Houthis in the strategic northern governorate of al-Jawf.

Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said on Sunday evening that government forces conducted 1,272 “targeting operations” against Houthi fighters, fortifications and weapons supplies over 24 hours.

Operations are ongoing in al-Jawf, neighbouring Marib and al-Bayda to the south, added al-Nazili. Government forces killed roughly 500 Houthi fighters and destroyed or disabled nearly 170 vehicles, equipment or heavy weaponry.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims.

In southwest Yemen, the Houthis continue to besiege the city of Taiz, blocking the entry of food, fuel and medical supplies, in what authorities warn is a mounting humanitarian crisis.

Taiz Governor Nabil Shamsan has called for urgent help for the city’s deteriorating health facilities. He said 120 health centres have stopped operating and another 66 are close to shutting down since the Houthis cut off supply routes to the city in early October.

Nour al-Din al-Mansouri, a member of the committee facilitating the work of the Taiz Siege Affairs Office, told Al Jazeera that at least 23 trucks were damaged or overturned in the past two weeks while seeking alternative routes to Taiz.

The city is Yemen’s third-largest and home to about one million of the country’s roughly 43 million people.

Full-scale fighting reignited in Yemen in September, when the Houthis made crucial gains that tightened their grip on the Red Sea coast.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a campaign called Operation Dawn of Yemen last month to regain Houthi-held sites and restore government control over other territories held by the group, which seized the capital Sanaa in 2014.

images.caption: Houthi fighters in al-Jawf, September 15, 2026 [Handout via Reuters]
A rubbish-strewn roadside in Taiz in Yemen [File: Anees Mahyoub/Reuters]

articles.title: The Voice UK winner Cate McHugh says she wanted to be Taylor Swift growing up
articles.summary: Cate McHugh has gone from busking on the streets of Cardiff to winner of The Voice UK.
articles.body:
The winner of the Voice UK says she decided "I was going to be Taylor Swift" as a teenager after being given a guitar, before busking on the streets of Cardiff.

Welsh singer Cate McHugh was crowned the winner of the show on Saturday , after being mentored by "the legend that is Sir Tom Jones".

McHugh, from Llantwit Major, in the Vale of Glamorgan, said Sir Tom was so warm and supportive that it felt "as if you've known him for years".

One of the standout pieces of advice he gave to her early on was to focus on the story being told in the song, she explained.

McHugh said that when she found herself getting "a little bit flappy and excited" while rehearsing Sir Tom would say "nope, what's the story?", and urged her to focus on that and "stay true".

The 32-year-old, who began her career as a teenager busking under the watchful eye of her parents, said she and Sir Tom had "really lovely interactions and a lovely comfortable connection" and that it was "just an honour to be in his presence".

The final was a poignant moment for Sir Tom as it was his last appearance on the show, having been a coach on and off since it began in 2012.

He made headlines in September after revealing that ITV had "made the decision" to "fire" him from the show's coaching panel .

McHugh said that in the moments before she was announced as the winner, she felt "super peaceful because I was so happy with where I'd come" in the show.

The singer, who has a six-year-old daughter and a 16-year-old stepson, said she felt confetti on her shoulder and "opened my eyes and thought 'oh my God, they said my name'."

She said she wanted to thank her family, including her husband Nathan, for surrounding her with "all of that love" and support throughout the show and during the final.

Recalling her early days of performing, McHugh said "I was the kid who was always singing and my parents decided very early on that if they didn't put me in singing lessons this was going to get really annoying really quickly".

She was gifted an acoustic guitar for her birthday around the time Taylor Swift released her album Fearless, and "decided that I was going to be Taylor Swift, I was going to learn the entire album from start to finish".

Aged 15, she told her parents she wanted to busk in Cardiff and "they did everything they could to fulfil that happening in the safest way which did mean, apparently, my father was lingering around on Queen Street, just keeping an eye on me".

Busking and taking requests from passers-by helped her to gain confidence and she has "paid my dues since then", including singing on cruise ships, McHugh said.

McHugh said that navigating losing her sight aged 22 due to degenerative macular condition Stargardt disease had made her more determined to succeed.

She said music had "always been an outlet, emotionally, as so many musicians will say, but for me, when I'm on a stage singing and the lights are down on the audience, it's the one place that I don't think about my sight loss".

McHugh said that "as long as I know the words and I'm not trying to read them off an iPad then I'm absolutely there in that moment".

She described her sight loss as "just a small part of me, it's not who I am".

McHugh added that while many people with differences and disabilities sometimes felt they had to make themselves smaller "so that you don't become a nuisance to people", she chose "to find a way to take up space and be bigger and that's where music took me".

She is now working on her first original song in a studio which should be released "relatively soon, hopefully, fingers crossed".

Footage shared by McHugh on social media after her win showed her laughing and smiling with family and friends screaming in delight as they celebrated her victory at a watch party in Cardiff.

She has won a £50,000 cash prize and a recording contract, with her first ever single, a cover of The Beatles classic Blackbird, now released.

articles.title: Yankees' Jazz Chisholm Jr. receives 'frustrating' free agent prediction from ESPN
articles.summary: Chisholm may have hurt his free agent market.
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. wanted to become the second player in Major League history to record a 50-50 season.

He stole 41 bases but managed just 19 home runs in his second full season with the New York Yankees .

It appears the Yankees will be moving on from Chisholm this offseason, as the second baseman is now a free agent. New York did not extend him the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Monday evening.

"Extending the qualifying offer (a one-year, $23.15 million deal) would have seemed easy on paper, but it's unclear how much enthusiasm the Yankees have for Chisholm, and I'm also not sure how much other teams will be pounding the table, as baserunning-and-defensive-heavy WAR totals often don't get paid in free agency, and on top of that, his xwOBA was a career worst," ESPN's Kiley McDaniel wrote.

McDaniel projects Chisholm to sign a two-year, $46 million contract this winter, well short of what the left-handed hitter believes he's worth.

In February, Chisholm told NJ.com's Randy Miller that he was looking for $35 million per year for eight to 10 years.

"What did I tell you last year? $300 million? It's probably bigger than that now, probably $35 million." Chisholm told Miller.

Well, the left-handed hitter certainly won't come anywhere close to that in his career. Chisholm still provides value with power and speed, but the flaws in his game (swing and miss, lack of focus) are hard to miss.

$46 million is way less than what Chisholm is hoping for, but he may have to accept that he lowered his value with his unbalanced performance this season with the Yankees.

articles.title: Bride Goes Viral After Challenging Groom to Beat Her at Valorant Before Marrying Her
articles.summary: A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant before they could officially marry.
articles.body:
A bride in China is going viral for giving her husband-to-be a wild challenge: making him beat her at Valorant before they could officially marry.

A video showing the couple facing off in Riot’s tactical first person shooter has racked up nearly three million views in just one day. In the clip, the bride — decked out in her wedding finery and delicate hair ornaments — takes virtual shots at her soon-to-be lawfully wedded opponent, who sits across from her while a group of friends and family look on in amusement.

While this is certainly a unique way to celebrate one’s nuptials, it isn’t totally out of the ordinary. In fact, pre-wedding challenges like these are actually part of Chinese culture. They’re called ‘door games,’ and they’re a playful, lighthearted way to prepare for the actual ceremony and following reception.

Traditionally, these are silly tasks organized by bridesmaids that the groom must successfully complete in order to ‘earn’ the right to actually marry his bride. They usually take place the morning before the wedding at the home of the bride’s family, and his groomsmen are often enlisted to help. It’s a symbolic way of making the groom ‘prove his worth’ before he takes the bride’s hand in marriage.

Door games can be anything the bridesmaids choose, really; according to China Insider, these generally involve tasks like eating unusual foods, athletic challenges like doing push-ups, or testing their knowledge with trivia. In this case, the bridesmaids decided to put his elite gaming skills to the test — and it went so viral that even the official Valorant Instagram account took notice.

“Wait, the wife is lowkey locked in,” it said in a comment.

“The problem is if he wins, she will remember it for life, and he would not hear the end of it, but if he doesn’t, it would be near impossible to find another gem like her,” one viewer joked, while another called it the true definition of “skill-based matchmaking.”

Even the CEO of pro esports team GAM commented, saying, “How do we sign her?”

This is the latest gamer wedding to go viral after a Pokémon fan was able to fund his wedding by selling a trio of rare Charizard cards that had been stored in his attic for a mind-boggling $44,000.

And in 2024, a streamer couple took social media by storm for their Black Ops 6-themed wedding that they held at the Call of Duty Next event in Washington, D.C. Now, that’s true love.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Lakers face Luka Doncic ‘malpractice’ warning as trade likelihood reaches 65%
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have been warned that failing to strengthen their roster around Luka Doncic would be a major mistake, with NBA insider Jovan Buha putt...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have been warned that failing to strengthen their roster around Luka Doncic would be a major mistake, with NBA insider Jovan Buha putting the chances of a trade at 65 per cent.

The Lakers have made an impressive 6-2 start to the season, largely thanks to Doncic's outstanding form. However, questions remain over their depth, particularly at centre and on the wing.

With the Western Conference looking increasingly competitive, Los Angeles could look to make additions before the trade deadline to improve its championship chances.

Jovan Buha says Los Angeles Lakers would be making a mistake by not trading

Speaking on his podcast, Buha's Block , the insider explained why the Lakers need to take advantage of Doncic's current form rather than leave gaps in the roster.

"If the Lakers don't make a move and don't try to improve this roster, it would be, to quote you, malpractice," Buha said. "I just think that would be a giant mistake having Luka in his prime, potentially the best season of his career, and to not improve a couple of holes in the roster."

Buha believes Los Angeles has a strong opportunity to compete in the West and should be prepared to act.

"Odds of making a trade, I would say like 65% right now," he added.

However, the insider does not necessarily expect the Lakers to make an immediate move. He suggested the franchise could wait until it has a clearer understanding of its rotation and where the biggest problems lie.

"If someone goes down, maybe there's a different need, or there's some urgency to do something, or if they just continue to struggle to navigate some of these bench groups, maybe they feel some urgency to get a center at some point in December," Buha said.

The Lakers have reportedly been looking for another centre to provide cover behind Walker Kessler, while an upgrade at starting forward is also among their priorities.

Doncic's form makes the situation particularly important. He is averaging 38.3 points, 8.1 assists and eight rebounds per game, putting himself firmly in the MVP conversation.

There is also a longer-term consideration. Doncic's current contract could run through 2028 or 2029, depending on his player option, and ESPN's Brian Windhorst has previously highlighted the importance of keeping the Lakers in a strong position to secure an extension.

For Rob Pelinka and the front office, the challenge is finding the right additions without rushing into a deal. But Buha's warning makes one thing clear: the Lakers cannot afford to waste Doncic's current form.

articles.title: Indonesian president’s chief of staff dismissed over alleged wiretapping
articles.summary: Gov’t says Listyo may have committed ‘treason’ after he is arrested and accused of wiretapping top officials’ phones.
articles.body:
The Indonesian president’s chief of staff has been fired for what the government says could be “treason” after he allegedly wiretapped phones with the help of two other serving police officers.

President Prabowo Subianto dismissed Listyo Sigit Prabowo on Wednesday, a day after police announced his arrest over allegations that he had illegally wiretapped phones belonging to several high-profile individuals, including the president and cabinet ministers.

Two other senior police officers were also arrested, including Ahrie Sonta Nasution, head of the legal division of the Indonesian National Police, according to local media.

“This was, of course, carried out by certain rogue individuals, and we are also of ‌the view that what was done may already fall into a category that can be considered an act tending towards treason,” presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi said on Wednesday.

“It also tends towards acts that endanger state interests and the safety of the nation’s leadership, including the safety of the head of state,” he said.

The unauthorised wiretapping allegedly took place from last year to this year while Listyo was serving as chief of the National Police, a position he held for five years before becoming the president’s chief of staff last month.

The suspects are also accused of trying to conceal their actions by ordering the deletion of files containing intercepted communications last month.

Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Indonesia’s senior minister for legal affairs, said the motive behind the alleged wiretapping has not yet been determined.

The operation was conducted “without any legal basis or without any investigative or inquiry process in accordance with applicable laws”, according to Asep Safrudin, the top detective in the National Police.

Also on Wednesday, the Indonesian military deployed more than 20,000 soldiers in the capital, Jakarta. It did not say whether the deployment was linked to the arrests.

The new deployments include marine and navy troops, as well as personnel from training centres and naval bases in Java and Lampung province.

Indonesian armed forces spokesperson Major-General Muhammad Nas said the troop movement was standard procedure for maintaining national security and territorial integrity.

“Troop deployments are a normal occurrence,” Nas said, adding that the military “must always be prepared to protect the entire nation and safeguard the integrity of the Republic of Indonesia”.

images.caption: Listyo Sigit Prabowo was chief of the Indonesian National Police for five years before becoming the president's chief of staff [File: AFP]

articles.title: Bruins' James Hagens Linked With Major Award After Hot Start to Rookie Season
articles.summary: Hagens leads all rookies in scoring. If he's able to maintain that pace through the end of the year, that should see him compete for the grandest honor a fir...
articles.body:
The Bruins are back where they belong, sitting just three points off the Hurricanes for first-place in the Eastern Conference. There are a host of players to credit for their surging start to the year. None are as young as James Hagens, however.

The newly-minted 20-year-old has been a key cog in Marco Sturm's lineup thus far, amassing the third-most points on the roster despite averaging the fifth-fewest minutes. Hagens is a star in waiting. Talking heads are starting to realize it, too.

Here's what you need to know about Hagens' hot start, including how it might land him in award contention come the end of the season.

James Hagens Linked With Major Award After Hot Start

Hagens placed third on the Daily Faceoff's Steven Ellis' Calder Trophy ladder. Ellis writes:

Hagens was a natural center throughout junior and college, but it's never easy for a young player to come in and take on the added responsibility as a rookie. So it's been nice watching Hagens thrive in a third-line role, where he has managed to put up 11 points through 15 games. That's about a 60-point pace, which would be the second-best output by a Bruins rookie of the 21st century.

Ellis cited Hagens' speed, two-way prowess and desire to carry the puck in the middle of the ice as reason for his early success. He ranks tied for first in goals, tied for second in assists and first in points among rookie skaters. He has also proven a formidable asset on Boston's power-play, anchoring a second-line unit that has helped the Bruins convert 20 percent of their opportunities with a man advantage.

Hagens trailed only Canadiens netminder Jacob Fowler and Red Wings winger Michael Brandsegg-Nygard on Ellis' list of Calder Trophy favorites through the opening fifth of the season. He has ample time to scale up that mountaintop — Hagens' two-way sensibilities should help him surge from his third-line post in the coming few months.

In other words, Hagens is already showing signs of stardom in his age-20 season. That could help him compete for some hardware very soon.

articles.title: Indy Showcase, new college volleyball event, to help kick off season in 2027. What we know
articles.summary: College volleyball continues to grow around the Circle City, and in 2027 it will bring a new event to the city that once hosted the Final Four.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — College volleyball is returning to Gainbridge Fieldhouse with a two-day early season showcase.

The Indiana Sports Corp. announced Wednesday evening that the Indy Showcase will feature a four-team event Aug. 28-29, 2027. Similar to the men's college basketball Indy Classic, the event will serve as a fundraiser supporting Sports Corp. missions, according to a release.

Indianapolis once hosted a Final Four in 1987 at Market Square Arena, and college volleyball returned downtown on Oct. 16, 2025 when Purdue beat Indiana in the Monon Spike Match , which drew 6,477 fans on a sectional volleyball night , no less. The explosion of college volleyball reaching the Circle City is perhaps not a surprise.

The inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament will be hosted at the nearby Fishers Events Center from Nov. 20-25.

"You can't keep up with the explosion right now that is volleyball," Purdue coach Dave Shondell said last season. "And I think that you, fortunately people in the media are finally getting behind it — whether it be TV or print or on the internet — but it's hard to keep up with all the things that are going on in the attendance records that are being broken. You watch it every night you want to on TV, so it's a great time to be in volleyball."

The Indy Showcase will have information at a later date about the four teams, match times and broadcast information. However, it will bring four matches downtown early in the season, a rising trend across the sport.

The AVCA First Serve Showcase has become popular with Big Ten members Wisconsin (in Milwaukee) and Nebraska being featured prominently. Other events have blossomed out of those successes, both in television viewership and attendance.

Consider Indiana played at the Broadway Block Party in Nashville this season, and Purdue played in the State Farm Volleyball Showcase at the Sanford Pentagon in South Dakota and the Paradise Invitational in the Bahamas. Both teams were part of the Big Ten/SEC challenge, too.

Aside from the college level, the Indy Ignite enter their third season as the state's lone professional volleyball team. They won the Major League Volleyball regular-season championship in 2026 and open the next season in January. The state also produces top talent for the college level through various high school and club programs.

Now, Indianapolis is getting involved with the Sports Corp. and its mission to make Indianapolis the women's sports capital of the world by 2050. Perhaps that means a Final Four in the near future.

articles.title: Major Australian retailer David Jones folds after 188 years in operation
articles.summary: The brand's 38 physical stores and online site will continue to operate while receivers review its operations.
articles.body:
David Jones, Australia's oldest department store chain, has gone into voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk.

It comes after years of financial struggles for the 188-year-old retailer - known locally as DJs - as customers desert traditional shops for online shopping.

David Jones's physical and online stores will continue to operate while receivers FTI Consulting review the company, said voluntary administrators McGrathNicol.

"David Jones is an iconic company and so many Australians have stories and memories of visiting DJ's stores," said its CEO Erica Berthold, adding the brand has a "well-developed plan" to "reset the business for the future".

Berthold thanked "customers, our team members and our partners for their continued support of David Jones through this period".

David Jones employs about 6,000 staff and has 38 physical stores, with 17 of those in Westfield shopping centres.

Hours before the board voted to go into administration, Scentre - which owns Westfield - said the retailer had not paid its rent for October and was "therefore in breach" of its tenancy agreement.

"We understand the current retail trading environment, rising costs, a significant and outdated retail footprint, and supply chain challenges have led to this point," said Christopher Hill from receivers FTI Consulting.

By appointing administrators and receivers, David Jones will get "breathing space" and a chance to restructure the business, Hill said.

For many Australians, David Jones - and its trademark black-and-white houndstooth design - represented luxury.

But its collapse signalled the "death knell" for the department store format, said Jana Bowden, who teaches marketing at Macquarie University's Business School.

"It was once the epitome of glamour shopping in Australia - the Aussie version of Harrods," she said, "a place you would go to see and be a part of the glitz and glamour, where you could marvel at all the premium luxury labels, and feel like you'd made it."

Visiting the flagship city stores in Sydney and Melbourne was also a ritual for many Australian families, especially to see the festive Christmas window displays.

"People would travel from hours away from the city just to see those windows and experience the magic," Bowden said, but in recent years, the brand had lost its shine.

"The city stores have retained their upper end airs and graces, but the suburban stores leave a lot to be desired – they're mundane, they lack excitement and there's definitely no glitz," she said.

During Queen Elizabeth II's first visit to Sydney in 1954, the then-27-year-old monarch attended a banquet dinner on the seventh floor of the Elizabeth St store, according to the Sydney Morning Herald.

images.caption: Australia's oldest department store, David Jones, has gone into voluntary administration

articles.title: Why Connor McDavid’s contract negotiations sparked major NHL debate: How his $25 million Edmonton Oilers extension could shape the team’s salary cap, roster flexibility and Stanley Cup ambitions
articles.summary: Explore how Connor McDavid's two-year, $25 million contract extension with the Edmonton Oilers could influence the team's salary cap management, roster flexibility, and pursuit of the Stanley Cup. Discover the significance of McDavid's decision to prioritize team success over a larger contract, and what this means for the Oilers' future plans and NHL contract negotiations.
articles.body: One of the biggest talking points in the NHL was Connor McDavid’s contract negotiations, which led to the Edmonton Oilers captain signing a two-year, $25 million extension on Oct. 6, 2025. The superstar decided to stay at his current $12.5 million average annual value (AAV) through the 2027-28 season instead of going for a much bigger paycheck or long-term deal.The decision attracted attention because McDavid is widely regarded as one of hockey’s elite players and could have commanded a substantially larger contract. His shorter agreement also gives him an opportunity to reassess his future while allowing Edmonton’s management to focus on building a roster capable of winning the Stanley Cup.How McDavid’s $25 million deal shapes Edmonton’s title hopesMcDavid’s extension was notable not only for its total value but also for the message it sent about his priorities. The two-year agreement is worth $25 million, with an AAV of $12.5 million, matching the annual cap hit of his previous eight-year contract.At the time of the announcement, the deal was viewed as a significant financial concession compared with what a player of his standing might have sought on the open market. McDavid could have pursued a longer agreement with a higher annual value, but he chose a shorter commitment that keeps his championship ambitions with Edmonton at the center of the discussion.Why Connor McDavid took a shorter dealMcDavid's decision demonstrates how much he values winning a Stanley Cup with Edmonton. The Oilers made it to the Stanley Cup Finals in 2024 and 2025, only to lose both times to the Florida Panthers. A shorter extension allows the organization to keep working towards the championship goal without tying up a big chunk of its future salary cap on one player for a few more years.The agreement also gives McDavid more control over his next career decision. Rather than committing to an eight-year deal, he has kept the possibility of testing unrestricted free agency after the 2027–28 season.This arrangement creates a different kind of pressure for both the player and the organization. McDavid has committed to two more seasons, while Edmonton must demonstrate that it can use its available resources to build a championship-caliber supporting cast.How Connor McDavid’s contract affects Oilers roster flexibilityThe financial structure of McDavid’s extension gives Edmonton a predictable $12.5 million annual cap charge for both seasons. That figure is important because the NHL salary cap limits how much a team can spend on its active roster. Keeping McDavid’s cap hit unchanged gives general manager Stan Bowman more room to manage contracts involving other key players.McDavid’s agreement is particularly significant alongside the contracts of Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard. Draisaitl signed an eight-year extension carrying a $14 million AAV, while Bouchard's contract also represents a major commitment to the Oilers' defensive core. The front office will have to plan carefully in managing those salaries, and McDavid’s deal.The organization has also tried to retain key defensive pieces. Jake Walman signed a seven-year extension in October 2025 worth $49 million and carrying a $7 million AAV. Edmonton then extended veteran defenseman Mattias Ekholm for three years at $12 million. Those kinds of deals show the team’s effort to keep continuity around its top players.What matters is the difference between McDavid's actual annual salary and his cap hit. His cap charge remains $12.5 million in both seasons, even though his signing bonuses and base salary are distributed differently. The contract also includes a full no-movement clause, giving him protection against being traded or moved without his consent.Why the Oilers must balance their championship rosterMcDavid's decision does not automatically guarantee that Edmonton will have enough room to sign every player it wants. The club still needs to consider contract renewals, player development, defensive depth and goaltending when planning its roster.However, retaining the captain at the same AAV provides a more predictable financial foundation than a substantially larger contract might have offered. It also allows the Oilers to keep investing in players who can contribute alongside McDavid and Draisaitl.The challenge for Bowman is to make those resources count. Edmonton has reached the Stanley Cup Final in consecutive seasons, but maintaining that level requires more than relying on its two leading forwards. Defensive consistency, reliable goaltending and contributions from the supporting lineup will all remain important.What Connor McDavid’s 2028 free agency means for EdmontonOne of the most significant aspects of the extension is its limited duration. McDavid's agreement runs through the 2027–28 season, after which he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent in 2028 at age 31.This gives the Oilers a defined period to demonstrate that their roster can compete for the championship. Should Edmonton show measurable progress, the organization may have the opportunity to negotiate another deal with its captain before he becomes an unrestricted free agent.The short-term nature also benefits McDavid by keeping his options open for negotiations. The NHL salary cap is going to keep moving, and a higher ceiling could open up opportunities for bigger contracts down the road. That does not guarantee that McDavid will leave Edmonton or sign a particular deal, but it gives him the freedom to evaluate his options when the current extension expires.What McDavid’s next contract could mean for the NHLMcDavid's decision has also raised questions about how superstar contracts influence negotiations across the league. His $12.5 million AAV is below a number of other top NHL players who have signed big deals, including Kirill Kaprizov’s $17 million AAV and Draisaitl’s $14 million AAV.His agreement is unusual because elite players usually have strong financial incentives to secure the maximum possible contract value. However, McDavid's situation also demonstrates that a player can prioritize team-building flexibility and a shorter commitment when considering his next career move.The Edmonton Oilers’ short-term goal remains the same: leverage their championship experience to win a Stanley Cup. McDavid has given management a solid cap number for two more seasons, but it is now up to the organization to build a competitive roster around him.At the end of the day, the extension is more than a $25 million deal. It’s a mutual commitment to another shot at a championship, while leaving the door open on McDavid’s longer-term future. How Edmonton capitalizes on that opportunity could shape the captain’s next contract decision and the franchise’s direction beyond 2028.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: MLW owner talks Tessa Blanchard, Masha Slamovich signings: 'I believe in forgiveness'
articles.summary: Major League Wrestling owner Court Bauer says Tessa Blanchard's arrival was a decade in the making after a 60-day delay pushed her debut to the PPV.
articles.body: It’s no secret Major League Wrestling (MLW) has brought in some big names into the company over the last few years with wrestlers like Killer Kross, Scarlett Bordeaux, Austin Aries, Trevor Lee, Shotzi Blackheart and several others being on the roster at one point or another. Two other notable names that caught the attention of the pro wrestling world this year bolstered MLW’s women’s division – Tessa Blanchard and Masha Slamovich (known in MLW simply as Masha). CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE Blanchard, a third-generation pro wrestler, has vehemently denied racism allegations for years even as she’s been featured as a top player in several promotions. Slamovich addressed domestic abuse allegations in September 2025, apologizing for her actions in what she described as a "mutually destructive relationship." MLW first announced Blanchard’s signing in September of this year and she was initially planned for Fightland. Some confusion pushed back her debut to Saturday Night SuperFight, which takes place this weekend and can be seen on Veeps. MLW owner Court Bauer addressed Blanchard’s signing in an interview with OutKick Dropkick. "There are things in this business that happen that are just unique and I really can't talk about it other than saying, ultimately what happened was you had about a 60-day delay on it and instead of her debuting in Charleston for a TV taping, she's arriving at our pay per view, which is a critically awesome moment for it to happen. So, it worked out pretty damn good for us and we're thrilled, CMLL's thrilled and Tessa's thrilled. I think that's all that matters. "But for Tessa, she's been an incredible part of the CMLL roster, and for her to come over is a huge honor and she was actually supposed to be a part of the original relaunch of MLW in 2017. We had taped stuff of her training and, again, it was one of those weird things where just the timing didn't work and it didn't happen. She was gonna be like one of the cornerstones of MLW at that point in time of our new era talents. And then here we are. That was 2017. Here we are 2026, end of 2026, almost 10 years later. And seeing all of this incredible success she's had in Mexico and she's had elsewhere and it's to come back and do this finally. It's about a decade in the making. So finally, it will not be denied, just like her undeniable. she's gonna be here." Bauer told Wrestling Observer Radio he was a believer in "second, third chances" for people. OutKick Dropkick asked Bauer if he share the same sentiment for Slamovich. MLW'S COURT BAUER TOUTS 'HUGE YEAR' FOR COMPANY AMID MEDIA DEALS, SPLASH MOVES "I believe in forgiveness," he said. "As a Christian, I believe in forgiveness. I think we're so quick to condemn and everyone gets executed and then they're just on the island of irrelevancy. They are to be forgotten. They are shunned forever, and there are definitely people in this world, in this business, that should be. And there's people in this business that could be, but there are a lot of people that make bad mistakes, terrible mistakes, and they repent, and they realize their errors and their things that they could have done differently. They're young people, they're living in a time where they're just on the go constantly, and then they get to settle down and they get to have perspective. But you gotta have the ability to see that and then you have a conversation with those folks, you see where they're at, and I'm not saying one person in particular, but my approach has always been, yeah, you know, give second chances, give forgiveness. "I mean, we're so easy to condemn and I think that's just something that if I hadn't had a second chance, third chance, fourth chance, I mean I really sometimes would make a mess when I was younger and you don't realize, you know, maybe this is it for me and thankfully people gave me another chance, and if they hadn't, I wouldn't be here. I wouldn't be in this position, and I'm grateful for that. "And so forgiveness to me is like one of those things that really I wish would get an equal amount of enthusiasm, especially on social media, versus quick to just let's go out there and let's get our pitchforks and torches and go burn that person down. And once they're torched, they're satisfied and that person's just devastated. Yeah, maybe rightfully, they should be in that moment, on a sabbatical, but let them, you know, it's not all or nothing. I think there's a little bit of nuance there, a little bit of gray area in there, and I think that's where it's important to like let them kind of go on their journey of realizing that and then see if there's a conversation we had when the timing is right, when it's appropriate. That's kind of how … I've never really spoken about that deeply, but that's really where I stand both my heart and in my mind about it." Blanchard and Slamovich will both be in action at Saturday Night SuperFight. Blanchard will square off against Keyra and Slamovich will take on Zamaya this weekend. articles.title: G2 Esports Parts Ways With Head Coach Luka 'Perkz' Perković After His 'Tweet Bomb' Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach, Luka "Perkz" Perković, following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.
articles.body:
G2 Esports has parted ways with its head coach and retired League of Legends player Luka "Perkz" Perković following divisive comments he made in a lengthy post on Twitter/X.

The 2,676-word-long tweet was published on November 4, 2026. Perković described it as his “first and last honest post in [the] last decade,” where he could “address some things honestly.” He explained that he’d written the statement to clarify his stance on certain topics “so that, at the very least, you can hate me for what I really stand for, and then that's completely fine by me.”

In the post, which he jokingly called a “tweet bomb,” Perković said he is not a fan of and does not endorse the Tate brothers in any way; claimed that “doesn’t really do politics” and has never “ever voted once” in his life; said he is not a fan of either Donald Trump or Kamala Harris; said he is a devout Catholic; denied being a “Putin fanboy” or being on the side of Russia in the war on Ukraine; and shared his stance on abortion, comparing it to “murder.”

“I don’t really do politics, nor have I even ever voted once in my life. I do have opinions, and I wish I was more educated on the topic, but the truth is I’m not, so I stay away from it,” he wrote. “There are some things I stand for, very simple things in life, but the only thing that is unshakeable for me, how it’s so widely accepted in public, is abortion. I cannot comprehend how people do not understand that is a muder, as life is created at conception. That is one view I will die by and never change.”

Perković also addressed his relationship with retired League of Legends pro and former G2 CEO Carlos "ocelote" Rodríguez Santiago, who stepped down from the company in 2022 after sharing a video of himself at a party with Andrew Tate. “Me standing up for Carlos publicly when he was being cancelled has nothing to [do] with all the things I’m all accused of supporting. Trafficking? Misogyny? Nazism? War? Are you okay?” Perković said of the matter.

“Carlos believed in me when nobody else did. I did not have a close relationship with my family when I was 16, including my parents, [who] I was not too close with, either. …Carlos and I have gone both completely different ways. He is his own person and I’m completely my own. In the end Carlos’ ego is something that put an end to his esports career, which was f**king insane. So there is a lesson to be learned in there, as well. We have a lot of different views on life.”

Perhaps the biggest takeaway from Perković’s post was his stance on abortion. This particular remark was a main talking point among fans and fellow players on social media, sparking a massive wave of backlash against him. G2 Esports addressed the situation in a public post mere hours later, where they confirmed that they have parted ways with Perković due to his tweet.

“Last night, like many of you, we saw the statement shared by the Head Coach of one of our teams. G2 is a diverse and international organization with different people from all around the world. While the world is complex and not everyone agrees on everything, some of the statements made last night do not align with G2's stance and values. We have fans with different cultures and personal opinions, and it is of the utmost importance to us as an organisation that we respect and uphold this diversity when representing G2. We acknowledge that this statement hurt many of our fans, and we want to apologize for it.

“As a result, we have decided to terminate our collaboration with the individual. We will now focus on rebuilding our staff and roster for the next season and ask for your patience, as we will not be able to communicate any changes until free agency officially opens. - Alban Dechelotte, CEO of G2.”

Perković has since published one other tweet — a Bible verse from Luke 6:22. “Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake,” he wrote. This post, too, has received backlash from users. Perković has not posted anything else on his account at the time of writing.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: MLW's Trevor Lee set for major high-stakes match against Yota Tsuji at Saturday Night SuperFight
articles.summary: Trevor Lee called out IWGP heavyweight champion Yota Tsuji for a massive showdown at MLW's Saturday Night SuperFight in Chicago this weekend.
articles.body: Trevor Lee officially signed with Major League Wrestling (MLW) seven months ago and he has kept his foot on the gas pedal since stepping in between the ropes for the company. Lee has gone toe-to-toe with some of the best MLW has to offer, including Kushida, Austin Aries and Místico, while also holding the MLW Southern Crown Championship. He broke the news with OutKick Dropkick/Fox News Digital in April and said at the time he had been waiting for a good opportunity to come his way. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE Now, he’s making the most of it. Lee will have a chance to make a statement at Saturday Night SuperFight this weekend when he steps into the ring with IWGP heavyweight champion Yota Tsuji, who is a superstar with New Japan Pro-Wrestling. "I think it’s been going great," Lee told OutKick Dropkick of his time with MLW so far. "I think with the last time we spoke, I probably said something along the lines of, I just want to go out there and show what I can do, and I feel like over these past few months, I've had the capability to do that. I think that we're gonna be looking at even more opportunity coming this Saturday when I wrestle Yota. I mean, I couldn't ask for a better opportunity, right? The IWGP heavyweight champion. I'm looking at this match like kind of like a job interview, right? And, what a way to, what a way to try to start it out." Lee was the one who called out Tsuji for this match at one of MLW’s biggest shows of the year. MLW'S COURT BAUER TOUTS 'HUGE YEAR' FOR COMPANY AMID MEDIA DEALS, SPLASH MOVES Tsuji is a two-time IWGP heavyweight champion, two-time IWGP global heavyweight champion and has held the IWGP Intercontinental Championship and the NEVER Openweight 6-Man Tag Team Championship one-time each. The stakes are as high as they could be going into this match. "I wanna show that I'm ready for that opportunity and if we're gonna bring these guys in and we're gonna highlight these guys as being the top guys that they truly are, Yota is the top of the top at New Japan," he continued. "So, if he's gonna come over here and he's gonna ask for a fight, then, you know, I'm looking for an opportunity. And I told you that right the last time we spoke, that I'm just wanting opportunities and what bigger opportunity." Tsuji already has a cast of wrestlers gunning for his title. Most recently, it was Boltin Oleg and Kenny Omega. Though Saturday night’s match is a non-title fight, the potential of Lee pinning Tsuji may put him among the contenders for the IWGP Heavyweight Championship. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! OutKick Dropkick asked Lee if he’s thought about that possibility. "One-hundred percent," he said. "I'd love to wrestle for New Japan. I've never wrestled for New Japan. I've wrestled for a lot of companies in, in my career, but, I've never had the opportunity to even go to Japan and wrestle in Japan. So, what better way to step in day one to show everybody, hey, I've already beat the top guy here and, and I'm ready to continue to do it again." Lee vs. Tsuji is one of seven matches on the massive Saturday Night SuperFight card, which will feature MLW world heavyweight champion Killer Kross going up against Josh Bishop in a last man standing match for the title. Lee predicted that the Chicago crowd will be "rocking" as MLW brings a different style of pro wrestling to the masses.
